Report_ID: Knee function (KF) score, change from baseline to 12 weeks
Title: Effectiveness of Patellar Bracing for Treatment of Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome
Author: Lun, Wiley, Meeuwisse, Yanagawa
Comment: Means/SDs entered are change-from-baseline scores (12 weeks minus baseline) as reported in Table 3; endpoint (12-week) means were EB 38 (8) and B 40 (7), baseline EB 36 (9) and B 33 (8). No test statistic, p value, or numeric CI is reported — the paper only states that 95% CIs showed no significant difference among the 4 groups. Per-group n values are subject counts from Table 2; the analysis unit was individual knees (186 knees from 129 subjects), a potential unit-of-analysis issue. Instrument is a modified Werner knee function scale (max 53), not the AKPS/Kujala; higher = better function. M_diff left empty because this is a 4-arm trial and the paper reports no direct two-group difference estimate.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Exercise and Brace (EB) – home exercise program plus patellar brace') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults (≥18 y) diagnosed with patellofemoral pain syndrome, recruited from the general population of Calgary
Recruitment source: University of Calgary Sport Medicine Centre referrals, Calgary-area family physician referrals, campus/fitness-facility advertising
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) change in knee function score from baseline to 12 weeks per treatment group (Table 3)
Outcome variable: Knee function (KF) score, change from baseline to 12 weeks
additional_group_ns: Arms reported but not used for this comparison: Exercise only (E) n=34, change 2 (10); Exercise and Sleeve (ES) n=31, change 5 (8)
unit_of_analysis: per knee (186 knees from 129 subjects) although group n reported per participant
outcome_units: points on modified Werner Knee Function Scale

Report_ID: Function score (Kujala Patellofemoral Score, 0-100) at 3 months
Title: Supervised exercise therapy versus usual care for patellofemoral pain syndrome: an open label randomised controlled trial
Author: van Linschoten et al.
Comment: SE_diff derived from the reported 95% CI of the adjusted difference: (9.72-0.14)/3.92 = 2.44. Group means/SDs at 3 months are for patients available at that time point (exact per-group analysed n at 3 months not reported for the function score; table header Ns 65/66 used). Adjusted difference is from a linear regression for repeated measures adjusted for baseline score, age, and duration of symptoms. Authors' "effect size" is the group difference divided by the baseline SD, not a conventional post-test SMD.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Supervised exercise therapy (plus standardised information)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: general practice and sport physician practice
Participant type: patients aged 14-40 with a new episode of patellofemoral pain syndrome
Recruitment source: 38 general practices (HONEUR network) and four sports medical centres, Netherlands
Outcome measurement: Self reported knee function questionnaire score, higher = better function
Outcome variable: Function score (Kujala Patellofemoral Score, 0-100) at 3 months
outcome_units: points on the 0-100 Kujala Patellofemoral Scale

Author: Fukuda TY, Rossetto FM, Magalhães E, Bryk FF, Lucareli PRG, Carvalho NAA
Comment: group_1/group_2 means and SDs are the 4-week POSTintervention values from Table 4. additional_group_ns: Knee and hip exercise (KHE) group, n=21 analysed, not included in this row (extracted separately as its own exercise-vs-control comparison)

Report_ID: Modified Kujala scale score (0-100, 100 = best function) at 6 weeks postintervention — SJNWBE vs control
Title: A Controlled Trial of Weight-Bearing Versus Non–Weight-Bearing Exercises for Patellofemoral Pain
Author: Herrington L, Al-Sherhi A
Comment: No numeric means, SDs, or standard errors are reported anywhere in the text or tables for the modified Kujala scale — values appear only in bar-graph Figure 1, which is an unreadable image. Only the p-value for the postintervention exercise-vs-control comparison is available (reported as P<.001; recorded as 0.001, an upper bound). No SMD/Hedges g can be computed from the reported data. Paired t tests with Bonferroni correction were used by the authors; the stated P<.001 is the postintervention between-group contrast reported jointly for SJNWBE and MJWBE vs control.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('SJNWBE: non–weight-bearing seated knee extension exercise, 3x/week for 6 weeks') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
domain: musculoskeletal physical therapy / patellofemoral pain syndrome
Participant type: Male patients (ages 18-35) with patellofemoral pain syndrome referred to a hospital physical therapy department
Recruitment source: Physical Therapy Department, Riyadh Armed Forces Hospital, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
Outcome measurement: Self-reported combined subjective and functional knee evaluation, 0-100 points
Outcome variable: Modified Kujala scale score (0-100, 100 = best function) at 6 weeks postintervention — SJNWBE vs control
additional_group_ns: MJWBE weight-bearing leg press arm, n=15, reported separately (see second row); total trial N=45
outcome_units: points on the modified Kujala scale

Report_ID: Lysholm scale score (functional ability) at 8 weeks — LP exercise vs no-exercise control
Title: Surplus Value of Hip Adduction in Leg-Press Exercise in Patients With Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Song CY, Lin YF, Wei TC, Lin DH, Yen TY, Jan MH
Comment: M_diff and 95% CI (5.60 to 15.87) are the paper's own between-group comparison of change (Table 3, LP vs Control); the CI numbers were placed in the generic ratio CI fields as the only available CI bucket for this mean-difference CI. SE_diff = (15.87-5.60)/3.92 = 2.62, derived from the reported 95% CI. Group means/SDs are post-intervention values from Table 2; Ns are randomized (intention-to-treat) Ns — completers were 27 (LP) and 25 (control). P reported only as "<.005".; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('LP group (leg-press exercise only)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: patients with patellofemoral pain syndrome, age ≤50 y
Recruitment source: referred to kinesiology laboratory by an orthopedic surgeon
Outcome measurement: Lysholm scale, 0-100 points, higher = better function
Outcome variable: Lysholm scale score (functional ability) at 8 weeks — LP exercise vs no-exercise control
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used in this row: LPHA group (hip adduction with leg-press exercise), n=29

Report_ID: Self-reported knee functional ability (WOMAC lower limb function score, change at 3 months)
Title: Physiotherapy for anterior knee pain: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Clark DI, Downing N, Mitchell J, Coulson L, Syzpryt EP, Doherty M
Comment: Values are pooled marginal (factorial) comparisons that the paper itself reports as a direct two-group contrast with its own mean difference and 95% CI; M_diff and CI taken verbatim from Table 4, not computed. WOMAC is scored so higher = worse function, so sign must be reversed for a "positive favours exercise" convention. CI bounds stored in the generic ratio CI fields as the only available CI slots for a mean difference. Group Ns derived from arm sizes (20+20 exercising; 19+22 non-exercising) reported in Tables 1-3.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Exercising patients (exercise+tape+education and exercise+education)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomised controlled trial (2x2 factorial, observer blind)
Participant type: patients aged 16-40 years with anterior knee pain of more than three months
Recruitment source: Orthopaedic and rheumatology consultants and general practitioners, City Hospital Nottingham
Outcome measurement: Change in WOMAC lower limb function score from baseline to three months (higher score = worse function; improvement = negative change)
Outcome variable: Self-reported knee functional ability (WOMAC lower limb function score, change at 3 months)
